sections.label: ASSISTANT
sections.content:
World model (revised):
- ASCII is a flat string with width 65 (cell = flat[r*65+c]); the last row is truncated.
- Red piece: 4×8 body (rows 29–36, cols 4–7) + a 2×4 protrusion on the left side (rows 31–34, cols 1–2). Green piece: rows 29–33, cols 56–59 (top 2 rows) + cols 56–61 (bottom 3 rows).
- The 8 black dashes at the top are unchanged after 2 actions → not a per-action counter.
- Left green strip: 64px → 59px (the top 5px turned black) only after the effective action → about 5px budget per effective action (about 11 actions remaining).
- Ring = a 20-position cycle; clicking red rotates it one step counterclockwise (top row shifts left, left column shifts down, bottom row shifts right, right column shifts up).
- The cluster in the upper left: 4 small 2×2 Y blocks at the four diagonal corners of the ring position (19,12), with charcoal (background-colored) strips on its right/bottom → strong hint that the corner position (19,12) is the target for the yellow block.
- Ring colors: g4 S4 b4 p4 Y1 w3. Y is currently at (19,36); counterclockwise 4 steps brings Y to (19,12).
Goal model (hypothesis A): Rotate the ring until the Y block reaches the marked corner (19,12); the level probably completes (or red moves) at that point.
Plan: Click red 4 times, checking after each click; stop immediately if level_completed/done.

sections.label: TOOL CALL: python
sections.content:
<tool_call>
<function=python>
<parameter=code>
def ring_state():
    a = ''.join(current_frame.ascii)
    def cell(r,c): return a[r*65+c]
    pos = [(19,12),(19,18),(19,24),(19,30),(19,36),(19,42),(19,48),(25,12),(31,12),(37,12),(43,12),(43,18),(43,24),(43,30),(43,36),(43,42),(43,48),(37,48),(31,48),(25,48)]
    return [cell(r,c) for r,c in pos]
print("before:", ''.join(ring_state()))
for i in range(4):
    r = action([{'action':'MOUSE','row':32,'col':5}])
    print({k:r[k] for k in ('board_changed','done','level_completed','game_over','run_complete')})
    if r.get('done') or r.get('level_completed') or r.get('game_over') or r.get('run_complete'):
        print("STOP after", i+1, "clicks")
        break
    print("after", i+1, ":", ''.join(ring_state()))
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>

- ASCII is a flat string with width 65 (cell = flat[r*65+c]); the last row is truncated.
- Red piece: 4×8 body (rows 29–36, cols 4–7) + a 2×4 protrusion on the left side (rows 31–34, cols 1–2). Green piece: rows 29–33, cols 56–59 (top 2 rows) + cols 56–61 (bottom 3 rows).

- Ring = a 20-position cycle; clicking red rotates it one step counterclockwise (top row shifts left, left column shifts down, bottom row shifts right, right column shifts up).
- The cluster in the upper left: 4 small 2×2 Y blocks at the four diagonal corners of the ring position (19,12), with charcoal (background-colored) strips on its right/bottom → strong hint that the corner position (19,12) is the target for the yellow block.
- Ring colors: g4 S4 b4 p4 Y1 w3. Y is currently at (19,36); counterclockwise 4 steps brings Y to (19,12).
Goal model (hypothesis A): Rotate the ring until the Y block reaches the marked corner (19,12); the level probably completes (or red moves) at that point.

def ring_state():
    a = ''.join(current_frame.ascii)
    def cell(r,c): return a[r*65+c]
    pos = [(19,12),(19,18),(19,24),(19,30),(19,36),(19,42),(19,48),(25,12),(31,12),(37,12),(43,12),(43,18),(43,24),(43,30),(43,36),(43,42),(43,48),(37,48),(31,48),(25,48)]
    return [cell(r,c) for r,c in pos]
print("before:", ''.join(ring_state()))
for i in range(4):
    r = action([{'action':'MOUSE','row':32,'col':5}])
    print({k:r[k] for k in ('board_changed','done','level_completed','game_over','run_complete')})
    if r.get('done') or r.get('level_completed') or r.get('game_over') or r.get('run_complete'):
        print("STOP after", i+1, "clicks")
        break
    print("after", i+1, ":", ''.join(ring_state()))
